correctness.rationale: The planar intersection-body radial function is the centered chord length in the perpendicular line. Its affine covariance ensures both |I(T-z)| and |T| scale by |det A|, so normalize triangle vertices to (1,0),(0,1),(-p,-q), p,q>0. For each slope m, intersections with the actual three edges yield the proof’s three rational branch formulas for the chord horizontal span d(m); polar area is exactly ∫_{−∞}^{∞} d(m)^2 dm. The given substitutions on negative, middle and positive intervals have elementary rational/log primitives and yield area S+2/S times the displayed symmetric log sum (S=1+p+q), equivalent to barycentric formula after dividing by S/2. Independently constructed raw line–segment intersections and quadrature, without using the provided d(m) branch code, at (p,q)=(1,1),(0.4,2.2),(4,0.12), matching areas 5.7725887222,5.6855004163,6.0450975291. For g(t)=t(1-t)log((1-t)/t), g′ is symmetric around 1/2 and strictly decreasing on (0,1/2); for any two distinct coordinates a>b with a+b<1, compare a to either b or 1-a to prove strict balancing increases ∑g. Evaluate g(1/3) and boundary pair g(t)+g(1-t)=0, proving the strict sharp bounds and all equality/limit cases. Quadrature is corroboration, not the universal proof.
residual_risks: Finite numerical corroboration is explicitly distinguished from the quantified analytic proof or exhaustive finite certificate.

value.rationale: A translated-center intersection-body area functional is an intrinsic, affine-invariant quantitative statistic of a simplex. The exact profile resolves the complete natural range, strict barycentric majorization, and unique centroid optimizer for all planar triangles; these are reusable extremal and geometric-functional facts not a manufactured finite slice. The boundary limit and affine normalization are structurally meaningful, even if higher-dimensional analogues are unknown.
residual_risks: Value assessment is mathematical usefulness of the precise new claim, not an assertion of broad downstream impact or publication prestige.

final_claim: For every nondegenerate triangle T and interior z with barycentric coordinates a,b,c>0 summing to 1, the planar intersection-body area ratio is 2+4sum_{t in {a,b,c}}t(1-t)log((1-t)/t). It is strictly Schur-concave on the three-coordinate simplex, with unique maximum 2+(8/3)log 2 at the centroid and continuous infimum 2 at every barycentric boundary point.
limitations: Strictly interior centers, nondegenerate planar triangles, ordinary area; lower endpoint is only the continuous boundary limit. No assertion about center outside or on boundary or higher-dimensional intersection bodies.
